The '''2022–23 Iowa Hawkeyes men's basketball team''' represented the [[University of Iowa]] during the [[2022–23 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]]. The team was led by 13th-year head coach [[Fran McCaffery]] and played its home games at [[Carver–Hawkeye Arena]] as members of the [[Big Ten Conference]]. They finished the season 19–14, 11–9 in [[2022–23 Big Ten Conference men's basketball season|Big Ten play]] to finish in a four-way tie for fifth place. As the No. 5 seed in the [[2023 Big Ten men's basketball tournament|Big Ten tournament]], they lost to No. 13-seeded [[2022–23 Ohio State Buckeyes men's basketball team|Ohio State]] in the second round. The Hawkeyes received an at-large bid to the [[2023 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] as the No. 8 seed in the Midwest region where the lost to [[2022–23 Auburn Tigers men's basketball team|Auburn]] in the First Round.

Junior forward [[Kris Murray]] earned First-team All-Big Ten honors and Third-team [[2023 NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|AP]], ''[[The Sporting News|Sporting News]]'' and [[United States Basketball Writers Association|USBWA]] All-America honors while averaging 20.2 points per game. It marked the fourth consecutive season that an Iowa player was named a consensus All-American, following twin brother [[Keegan Murray]] in [[2021–22 Iowa Hawkeyes men's basketball team|2022]] and [[Luka Garza]] in [[2020–21 Iowa Hawkeyes men's basketball team|2021]] and [[2019–20 Iowa Hawkeyes men's basketball team|2020]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Iowa Basketball: Kris Murray named consensus all-American |url=https://247sports.com/college/iowa/Article/Iowa-Basketball-Kris-Murray-named-consensus-all-American-207448025/ |publisher=[[247Sports]] |last=Eickholt |first=David |date=March 28, 2023 |access-date=March 29, 2023}}</ref>

==Previous season==
The [[2021–22 Iowa Hawkeyes men's basketball team|Hawkeyes]] finished the [[2021–22 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2021–22 season]] 26–10, 12–8 in [[2021–22 Big Ten Conference men's basketball season|Big Ten play]] to finish in a three-way tie for fourth place. The 26 wins were the most wins in a season for Iowa since the [[Elite Eight]] team in [[1986–87 Iowa Hawkeyes men's basketball team|1987]] earned 30 wins. As the No. 5 seed in the [[2022 Big Ten men's basketball tournament|Big Ten tournament]], they defeated [[2021–22 Northwestern Wildcats men's basketball team|Northwestern]], [[2021–22 Rutgers Scarlet Knights men's basketball team|Rutgers]], [[2021–22 Indiana Hoosiers men's basketball team|Indiana]], and [[2021–22 Purdue Boilermakers men's basketball team|Purdue]] to win the tournament championship. As a result, the Hawkeyes received the conference's automatic bid to the [[2022 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] as the No. 5 seed in the Midwest region. The Hawkeyes were upset by No. 12-seeded [[2021–22 Richmond Spiders men's basketball team|Richmond]] in the First Round.<ref>{{cite web |title=1 team from each NCAA men's basketball tournament bracket seed line to pick — and why |url=https://www.ncaa.com/news/basketball-men/article/2022-03-15/1-team-each-ncaa-mens-basketball-tournament-bracket-seed-line-pick-and-why |publisher=[[National Collegiate Athletic Association|NCAA]] |last=Wittry |first=Andy |date=March 15, 2022 |access-date=April 5, 2022}}</ref>

Sophomore forward [[Keegan Murray]] earned [[2022 NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|consensus First-team All-American]] honors, and established a new [[Iowa Hawkeyes men's basketball statistical leaders#Scoring|school record for points in a season]]. It was the third consecutive season that an Iowa player was selected a consensus First-team All-American ([[Luka Garza]], 2019–20 and 2020–21) and set a new school record for points in a season.
